style_when: the article describes one decisive moment or place — a yard at dawn, a control room, a shutdown line, a handover — that a film still could hold
prompt: Cinematic film still, 35mm anamorphic wide lens with dramatic falloff. Asymmetrical wide composition, hero object off-centre. A massive, modern white-enamel condensing water heater stands in an unfinished residential basement. Thick, pristine matte white PVC venting pipes jut aggressively from the unit, routing across a weathered, heavily textured concrete wall. Illuminated by a single harsh, amber workman's site lamp that casts long, deep shadows across the brushed metal utility panels. Restrained teal-and-amber color palette, crisp atmospheric depth, heavy material contrast between the new plastic venting and the old stone foundation.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, typography, text, words, human faces, people
rationale: A cinematic still frames the physical reality of the retrofit trap—the sheer scale of the new equipment and venting required in a typical, aging residential basement—using dramatic lighting to emphasize the unexpected capital burden.
subject: A modern condensing water heater with prominent new PVC venting pipes in a basement.
core_thesis: Replacing a gas water heater above 75,000 Btu/hr is no longer a simple swap but a major capital retrofit requiring new venting and condensate drainage.
core_conflict: Capital upgrade costs and complex retrofits versus simple like-for-like replacement budgets.
composition: asymmetrical wide shot with off-centre hero placement
